items.explanation: The tool says a secret key is written directly in the plugin source. Anyone who installs or reads the plugin could copy it and use the account behind it.
items.claim: Hard-coded API key literal `sk_live_EXAMPLE...` in property apiKey.
items.fix: Read the key at runtime: property string apiKey: Quickshell.env("ACME_WEATHER_KEY") || "" and document the variable in the README.

items.explanation: The tool says text from the model is shown as rich text. If a note title contained HTML such as a link or image tag, it would be rendered instead of shown as plain text.
items.fix: Use textFormat: Text.PlainText, or escape the title before building the markup.

items.explanation: The tool says the script downloads a script from the internet and runs it straight away. If that file ever changed, the plugin would run whatever it contains on the user's machine.
items.claim: curl | bash from an unpinned branch URL.
items.fix: Download a tagged release, verify its sha256, then run it: curl -fsSLo install.sh <url>@<tag>; echo '<sha256>  install.sh' | sha256sum -c -; bash install.sh

items.explanation: The tool says the plugin edits a file in the user's own Hyprland settings. That changes the user's setup outside the plugin's folder.
items.fix: Ask the user first, or write to the plugin's own data directory and tell the user to include it.

items.explanation: The tool says the plugin id is not specific enough. Two plugins with the same id would clash in the plugin list.
items.fix: Use a namespaced id such as io.github.<owner>.clock.

items.explanation: The tool says a timer runs every second. Whether this matters depends on how much work happens each second.
